# Pesher Psalms Column 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QpPs (4Q171), Col. 2 | **Condition:** moderate damage

---

**2:1** "The wicked-one draws-out his sword and bends his bow to bring-down the poor-one and the needy-one,

**2:2** to slay those whose way is upright" (Psalm 37:14).

**2:3** Its pesher concerns the wicked-ones of Ephraim and Manasseh, who will seek to stretch-out

**2:4** a hand against the priest and the men of his council in the time of trial that is coming

**2:5** upon them. But God will redeem them from their hand, and afterward

**2:6** they shall be given into the hand of the ruthless-ones of the nations for judgment.

**2:7** "Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows

**2:8** shall be broken" (Psalm 37:15).

**2:9** Its pesher concerns the wicked-ones of [...who] plotted to destroy

**2:10** the poor-ones [...] but God will redeem them and [...] the wicked-ones

**2:11** shall perish [...].

**2:12** "Better is the little of the righteous-one than the abundance

**2:13** of many wicked-ones" (Psalm 37:16).

**2:14** Its pesher [...] the Teacher of Righteousness, who [...]

**2:15** God establishes [...] his inheritance, for [...]

**2:16** [...] the congregation of His chosen-ones [...]

**2:17** [...] like a planting of [...]

---

*EMET notes: Translated from 4Q171 Col. 2. "Wicked-ones of Ephraim and Manasseh" — sectarian code names, likely for the Pharisees and Sadducees respectively. "The priest" — likely refers to the Teacher of Righteousness. "Ruthless-ones of the nations" (aritsei ha-goyim) — preserved as literal compound. Column becomes increasingly fragmentary from line 14 onward.*
